description: The plot titled “Training Loss of 20M Data Size” illustrates how training loss changes over training steps for six model configurations at a 20M data size. The x-axis is labeled “Step” on a linear scale and is shown with a broken axis: the main segment runs from 0k to 80k with tick labels at 0k, 20k, 40k, 60k, and 80k, and a second segment runs from 420k to 440k with tick labels at 420k, 430k, and 440k. The y-axis is labeled “Train Loss” on a linear scale; the main panel spans from 0.0 to 0.75 with labeled ticks at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, and 0.75, and there is a small upper strip indicating values around 0.75 to 0.85 (with a labeled tick at 0.85). Six solid lines without markers are shown: ChemBART Small 20M (red) starts near the upper range (around ~0.8) at the earliest steps, drops steeply within the first few thousand steps, then continues a gradual decline to roughly the low ~0.1 range by ~80k, and appears around a few hundredths (roughly ~0.03–0.05) in the 420k–440k segment; ChemBART Medium 20M (blue) follows a similar shape, beginning near ~0.8, decreasing rapidly early, then tapering to around ~0.1 by ~80k and sitting around a few hundredths in the 420k–440k segment; ChemBERTa Small 20M (green) begins near ~0.8, declines sharply early, then decreases more slowly and remains higher than the other traces through much of 0–80k (ending around the mid ~0.1 range), and is around roughly ~0.05–0.06 in the 420k–440k segment; ChemBERTa Medium 20M (orange) starts near ~0.8, drops quickly early, then gradually declines to around ~0.1 by ~80k and is around a few hundredths (roughly ~0.04–0.05) in the 420k–440k segment; ChemLLaMA Small 20M (purple) starts near ~0.8, decreases steeply early, then continues downward to around ~0.08–0.1 by ~80k and is around roughly ~0.03–0.04 in the 420k–440k segment; ChemLLaMA Medium 20M (brown) also starts near ~0.8, drops rapidly at the beginning, then tapers to the lowest trace by ~80k (around ~0.07–0.09) and appears near roughly ~0.02–0.03 in the 420k–440k segment, with all lines showing small high-frequency fluctuations around their downward trends.
